newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-WARNE RIPS APART ENGLAND BATTING.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WARNE RIPS APART ENGLAND BATTING.

text.p: Leg-spinner Shane Warne took five wickets to rip the heart out of England's batting on the second day of the third test and leave Australia poised to take a healthy first innings lead.
Only a stubborn, unbroken ninth-wicket stand of 38 between Mark Ealham (23 not out) and Andy Caddick (14 not out) spared England being in even greater trouble.
By the close they had taken England to 161 for eight, still 74 runs adrift of Australia's first innings 235.
Warne took three for one in 26 balls at one stage and finished with five for 38.

England prospered at the start of their innings after losing captain Mike Atherton cheaply and had reached 74 for one before they collapsed to Warne's spin and crumbled to 123 for eight before Ealham and Caddick staged a minor recovery.
Opener Mark Butcher (51) and Alec Stewart (30) had made batting look easier as the pitch dried out, but Warne tipped the balance back to Autralia, who are 1-0 down in the six-match series.
